deviation: The draft has no requirement to execute a Data Processing Agreement before personal data is processed, which the playbook treats as mandatory with no fallback. It also weakens the standard: security measures are only what the Supplier "considers appropriate", breach notice is limited to "confirmed" breaches with assistance at Arcadia's cost, subcontractors are pre-authorised without notice or flow-down terms, and deletion excludes routine backups. Together these leave customer and employee data under weaker controls.
suggested_text: 8.1 The Supplier shall process Personal Data only on the Customer's documented instructions and in accordance with applicable data protection law. 8.2 The Supplier shall execute the Customer's Data Processing Agreement before any Personal Data is processed, and no Personal Data shall be processed, and the Services shall not go live, until it has been executed. In the event of conflict, the Data Processing Agreement prevails over this clause 8. 8.3 The Supplier shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, as set out in the Data Processing Agreement, to protect Personal Data. 8.4 The Supplier shall notify the Customer without undue delay of any actual or suspected Personal Data breach, and shall provide all information and assistance the Customer reasonably requires, at the Supplier's cost. 8.5 The Supplier shall not engage any subcontractor to process Personal Data without the Customer's prior written authorisation, shall bind each subcontractor to terms no less protective than this Agreement and the Data Processing Agreement, and remains fully liable for their acts and omissions. On termination or expiry, the Supplier shall delete or return all Personal Data at the Customer's choice and certify deletion in writing, except where retention is required by law.
